summary.text: A 30-year-old primigravida at 34 + 6 weeks’ gestation was transferred for management of PPROM. Her history included allergic rhinitis and diet-controlled gestational diabetes; she denied smoking, alcohol and drug use. One week before admission she had a first, mild SARS-CoV-2 infection with rhinitis only, and she had completed full COVID-19 vaccination four years earlier.
Before transfer she received dexamethasone 6 mg intramuscularly and intravenous ritodrine; on arrival ritodrine was replaced with atosiban and broad-spectrum antibiotic prophylaxis was started.

On admission she was afebrile and normotensive with headache and no abdominal pain, visual disturbance, jaundice or oedema; GCS was 15/15. Ultrasound showed a single live cephalic fetus with oligohydramnios, estimated fetal weight 2000 g and normal Dopplers; initial laboratory tests showed markedly elevated transaminases and cholestatic enzymes, coagulopathy and renal impairment, with urinary sediment indicating acute tubular necrosis. Table 1 gives serial laboratory values from admission to discharge.

About five hours after admission she developed new dyspnoea with further rises in creatinine and worsening coagulopathy. Because of rapidly deteriorating hepatic and renal function an urgent caesarean section delivered a live male infant of about 2000 g who required neonatal intensive care.

Postoperatively she was admitted to the ICU with severe metabolic lactic acidosis (lactate 8 mmol/L) and respiratory decompensation. Liver and renal function improved steadily; repeat ultrasound on postoperative day 5 showed diffuse hepatic steatosis, and abdominal CT showed no findings. She was discharged from the ICU six days after admission and from the hospital 12 days after, with highly improved laboratory parameters.

Concern was raised for AFLP, atypical or normotensive HELLP syndrome and possible COVID-19-related hepatic injury; AFLP was the leading diagnosis and HELLP remained a differential. The neonate had initially elevated liver enzymes and prolonged coagulation times but recovered with supportive management.
